disclaimer: Programme availability, cohort dates, prices, fund strategies, and application criteria change frequently. Verify the current terms with each official source before applying, investing, relocating, or budgeting.
amount_convention: Amounts retain the currency published by the official source. No exchange-rate conversions are inferred.
accelerators_note: The accelerators array is a legacy finder category that also includes incubators, innovation ecosystems, and challenge programmes. Each record states its actual programme type and cost status.
government_programs_note: The grants array is a legacy API key. Its records include non-financial support, equity investment, credit guarantees, and loans; they are not necessarily grants.
full_review_note: Full record-by-record primary-source review completed 2026-08-14. Every retained field and exclusion was reviewed; unsupported tickets and mandates were removed, live Hub71 and Dubai SME deadlines and DFDF metrics were refreshed, misclassified entries were moved to exclusions, and Bedayat was added.

accelerators.name: in5
benefits: Subsidized Dubai Development Authority licence and workspace options
Mentorship and investor introductions
Workshops, networking, and specialized facilities
No equity taken and no direct funding provided by in5
accelerators.application_process: Online application followed by steering-committee review; no fixed year-round availability claim is made.

pricing_snapshot.personnel_sponsorship_agreement_waiver: Waived for up to four visas during the first three years; establishment-card and visa charges remain payable.
pricing_snapshot.note: Published subsidized prices are not a free licence, office, or visa package. Third-party charges and terms can change.

accelerators.name: Hub71 Access Programme
accelerators.operator: Hub71, backed by Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development and Mubadala and based in ADGM
benefits: AED 250,000 in flexible in-kind incentives
AED 250,000 cash in exchange for equity through a SAFE
High-performing startups committed to Abu Dhabi may receive a further AED 250,000 cash for additional equity
Access to service providers and Hub71's corporate, government, and investor ecosystem

current_cohort.post_deadline_note: Applications submitted after the Cohort 20 deadline are considered for the next cohort.

accelerators.relocation_requirement: At least one founder is expected to relocate long-term and build a team in Abu Dhabi.
accelerators.equity_terms_note: The official programme pages state that cash is provided through a SAFE in exchange for equity but do not publish a universal valuation cap, discount, or equity percentage.

accelerators.name: DIFC Innovation Hub
benefits: Innovation Licence route for qualifying technology and innovation businesses
Workspace and access to an innovation ecosystem
Partner-specific innovation programmes whose terms vary

pricing_snapshot.note: An Innovation Licence does not authorize regulated financial services; separate DFSA authorization is required where applicable.

accelerators.programme_status_note: The current Innovation Hub page lists partner-specific programmes. No current general DIFC FinTech Hive cohort was verified.

accelerators.name: Dtec
benefits: Coworking and office options
Dubai Silicon Oasis licence and company-setup support
Community events, workshops, and mentoring

pricing_snapshot.note: Displayed year-one plans are paid. Funding opportunities, where available, are separate and are not guaranteed by taking a Dtec workspace or licence.

accelerators.name: Dubai Future Accelerators
accelerators.cost_status: No universal public participation fee, equity term, or cash-award term was verified; terms are challenge-specific.
benefits: Connections to participating government and private-sector problem owners
Challenge-specific co-creation, validation, and potential pilot opportunities
accelerators.application_status: The official page lists open challenges; eligibility, deliverables, and commercial terms vary by challenge.

accelerators.name: Sheraa S3
accelerators.free_status_scope: No participation fee and no equity. The first-year SRTIP licence and coworking are covered, but selected startups must maintain a Sharjah licence for at least two years and later licence costs are not covered.
benefits: Growth support, mentorship, and ecosystem access
First-year SRTIP licence and coworking

current_status.note: The official page explicitly describes S3 as neither an incubator nor an accelerator. No later public application cycle was verified.

accelerators.name: Bedayat Incubator and Accelerator
accelerators.cost_status: No universal public participation fee, equity, or cash-funding terms were verified.
benefits: Sustainability-focused programmes and workshops
Living Lab testing and validation
Mentor and ecosystem connections
Facilitation of access to grants and funding without a funding guarantee
accelerators.application_status: An official application form is available; no fixed public cohort deadline was verified.
accelerators.eligibility_note: Applicants should address The Sustainable City's social, environmental, or economic sustainability pillars and cannot simultaneously participate in another incubator or accelerator.

accelerators_excluded_with_reason.name: AREA 2071
accelerators_excluded_with_reason.reason: The current Dubai Future Foundation page describes a co-creation and innovation space with facilities and startup-licence support, not a discrete accelerator with a fixed cohort or funding offer. It is excluded from the accelerator finder to avoid misclassification.

accelerators_excluded_with_reason.name: AstroLabs
accelerators_excluded_with_reason.reason: AstroLabs currently presents paid market-entry, business-setup, growth, and workspace services rather than a general open funding accelerator. It is excluded from the accelerator finder; individual market-entry programmes have their own terms.

vcs.name: BECO Capital
vcs.stage_scope: Fund IV invests from pre-seed through Series A; the Growth Fund invests from Series B through pre-IPO.

vcs.name: Wamda Capital
vcs.stage_scope: The active Wamda Seed vehicle targets sector-agnostic Seed to Series A technology startups. Fund I is fully deployed and harvesting.

current_fund.name: Middle East Venture Fund IV
current_fund.stage_note: The current Fund IV index does not publish a concise round-stage mandate.

vcs.name: Shorooq Partners
vcs.stage_scope: The current equity page says Shorooq invests across diverse stages and explicitly says it can invest as early as idea or pre-seed; it does not publish a single firm-wide round range.

vcs.name: Global Ventures
vcs.stage_scope: The current official site describes a growth-stage focus; Series B+ is a finder normalization, not a quoted round boundary.

vcs.name: COTU Ventures
vcs.stage_scope: COTU aims to be the first institutional cheque, investing as early as pre-seed, mostly at seed, sometimes at late seed, and rarely entering at Series A.
vcs.ticket_scope: Initial cheque; additional capital is reserved for follow-ons.

vcs.name: 500 Global MENA
vcs.stage_scope: The regional platform spans multiple dedicated funds and programmes. Its current overview describes team experience from pre-seed to pre-IPO, not one universal active-fund stage mandate.

vcs.name: Mubadala Capital Ventures
vcs.stage_scope: The Ventures platform backs early- and growth-stage companies; no universal round boundary or ticket is published on the current overview.

vcs.name: VentureSouq
vcs.stage_scope: Stage is fund-specific and is not stated on the current manager overview; the Global Seed Fund is marked deployed.
vcs.manager_location_note: MENA-based manager with a global portfolio.

vcs.name: Nuwa Capital
vcs.stage_scope: The current portfolio groups companies as Early and Growth but the current site does not publish a precise firm-wide round or ticket mandate.

vcs.name: RAED Ventures
vcs.stage_scope: The current application page says early-stage companies; exact round bounds and a universal ticket are not published.

vcs_excluded_with_reason.name: Cypress Growth Capital
vcs_excluded_with_reason.reason: Its current investment criteria require a US-headquartered B2B software or technology-enabled services company. Its royalty-based growth capital is not a MENA-focused VC mandate.

vcs_excluded_with_reason.name: Techstars Dubai
vcs_excluded_with_reason.reason: No Dubai accelerator appears in Techstars' current official accelerator or location directory. A separate Emirates NBD AI and fintech Acceleration-to-Enterprise partnership was announced on 2026-07-07, but no public open Dubai cohort with standard accelerator terms was verified.

innovation_accelerator.eligibility_summary: Market-stage or later innovators with a UAE presence or an intention to establish one; programme selection criteria apply.
innovation_accelerator.application_status: The official site has a live Apply call to action but publishes no dated cohort deadline.
innovation_accelerator.summary: Members receive coaching, expertise, partner and investor connections; neither the Accelerator nor MBRIF provides members direct funding.

guarantee_scheme.summary: A separate programme that facilitates bank finance through a government-backed credit guarantee. Accelerator membership does not guarantee support from the scheme.

current_portfolio_listing_snapshot.method: Derived count of entries on the official current portfolio listing.
current_portfolio_listing_snapshot.reconciliation_note: The live listing is newer and uses a different snapshot than the 2025 annual-report headline; the two totals are intentionally not merged.

grants.name: Dubai SME / Dubai Founders HQ
grants.operator: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism

hi2_tech_incubator.eligibility_summary: UAE resident aged 18 or older; at least one Emirati co-founder or team member; a technology idea or MVP less than two years old; full programme commitment required.

mohammed_bin_rashid_fund_for_smes.eligibility_summary: The current registration route states 100% UAE-national ownership and management, a project under five years old, applicant age 21 or older, and credit-scheme conditions.

grants.name: Khalifa Fund for Enterprise Development
grants.funding_eligibility_summary: Emirati entrepreneurs aged 21 to 60 with an operational business in Abu Dhabi emirate; product-specific criteria and final approval apply.

funding_products_snapshot.note: Agriculture and scale-up facilities are also listed. Limits, cost-coverage ratios, repayment periods, and eligibility vary by product.
